With roughly 7,636 residents age 65 and older, Dallas County is 32nd among 67 Alabama counties for older residents. That group is 21.1% of its population, compared with 18.3% across Alabama. The 2,738 residents now between 60 and 64 will become Medicare-eligible soon, and our turning 65 guide walks through it. Among residents 65 and older, 60% are 65 to 74, 31% are 75 to 84 and 9% are 85 or older (Census 2023 estimates). Medicare Advantage enrollment in Dallas County is 71.3% of people with Medicare, higher than the Alabama average of 61.5%. A county average does not tell you which kind of plan fits you. Whether Medicare Advantage or Original Medicare with a Medigap plan is the better fit depends on your doctors, your prescriptions and how you want to handle costs, so we compare both for your ZIP code.

Schedule a Medicare review

Booking opens Luay’s page on PlanEnroll. Create your profile there and ask for your meeting. Having these ready makes the first conversation useful:

  • Your Medicare card, or the dates your Part A and Part B start.
  • The doctors and hospitals you want to keep.

When PlanEnroll asks what type of meeting you would like, choose Health. You may be asked to complete a short Scope of Appointment form first. It does not obligate you to enroll. The first open time is at least 24 hours ahead. To talk sooner, call (301) 615-8289 or text (571) 354-0146.

Who has Medicare in Dallas County

Dallas County is a non-metro county with towns and small cities (USDA: urban population of 20,000 or more, adjacent to a metro area). Care is often split between local providers and a bigger hospital elsewhere, which is worth testing against each plan’s network.

CMS counts 10,139 Medicare beneficiaries in Dallas County (2023). Their average age is 71, about the same as the Alabama average of 72. About 32% are “dual eligible,” meaning they have both Medicare and Medicaid, higher than the state figure of 14%. Where many people have both, special plans for dual-eligible members can matter; see our Medicaid and dual eligible guide, since availability varies by plan and area.

Among people in Original Medicare in Dallas County, CMS reported about 643 emergency room visits and 289 inpatient hospital stays per 1,000 beneficiaries in 2023, which is close to the state average for emergency visits (600) and higher than it for hospital stays (247). About 9% received home health care. These figures describe how people use care under Original Medicare; they do not show what any plan covers or costs.

Sources: CMS Medicare Geographic Variation, 2023; USDA Rural-Urban Continuum Codes, 2023.

Medicare Advantage and Part D plan availability and provider networks are set county by county, so the plans open to you in Dallas County may differ from those in a neighboring county. We are not based in Dallas County; we help Dallas County residents by phone or video call.

Hospitals located in Dallas County

The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) lists this hospital in Dallas County:

  • Vaughan Regional Medical Center Parkway Campus — Selma (acute care; for-profit; emergency services; CMS overall rating 2 of 5)

A hospital being in the county does not mean every plan covers it. Medicare Advantage networks differ by plan, so we check the hospitals and doctors you actually use before you enroll. Ratings are CMS Care Compare overall hospital star ratings; they describe the hospital, not whether a plan covers it. Source: CMS Hospital General Information.

Dallas County: communities and ZIP codes

People in Dallas County live in communities such as Selma (16,666), Valley Grande (3,982), Orrville (143) (2023 population estimates, counting only the part of each community that lies inside the county).

We look up plans by ZIP code. In Dallas County, that means areas such as 36701, 36703, 36759, 36761, 36767, 36773, 36775, based on Census ZIP Code Tabulation Areas that lie mostly in the county.

Common questions

Dallas County Medicare FAQ

Can I get help with Medicare in Dallas County by phone?
Yes. Phone and video appointments are how we serve Dallas County. We hold a Alabama license, compare plans from many carriers and walk you through them from home, with no pressure to enroll.
Will my Dallas County doctors and hospitals be covered?
On a Medicare Advantage plan it depends on that plan’s network, so before you enroll we check whether your doctors and the hospitals you use, such as Vaughan Regional Medical Center Parkway Campus, are in network. With a Medicare Supplement (Medigap) plan you can see any doctor who accepts Medicare.
How many people in Dallas County have Medicare Advantage?
CMS reported 7,227 people enrolled in a Medicare Advantage plan out of 10,132 people with Medicare in Dallas County in September 2026, or 71.3%. The Alabama average was 61.5%.
Do you charge Dallas County residents for help?
No. You pay nothing to work with us. Carriers compensate us, and the price of your plan is the same as if you enrolled directly.
When can I enroll or change plans?
You can enroll during your Initial Enrollment Period around your 65th birthday, during the Annual Enrollment Period from October 15 to December 7, or during a Special Enrollment Period if you have a qualifying event such as moving into or within the county.
